title: Audit: standardize request_id/trace_id propagation and include correlation fields on emitted events
author: Caleb Johnson
release_notes: Audit events now include request_id and trace_id consistently across gateway + control plane services. Services propagate x-request-id and W3C traceparent headers end-to-end; audit emitter fills correlation fields automatically when present.
body:
Context: As part of the audit logging standardization work (schema v1 + sensitive action coverage), we need correlation identifiers to be present on every audit event so customers and internal responders can pivot from an API/Console action to the corresponding traces, logs, and downstream service calls. Today we have a mix of x-request-id, requestId, and trace-only correlation depending on service, and some async flows drop context entirely.

What this PR does: (1) Standardizes request_id propagation via x-request-id across internal HTTP hops, and ensures it is echoed back on gateway responses. (2) Standardizes trace_id extraction from W3C traceparent when present (OpenTelemetry), and ensures we always have a stable trace_id in request context when a span exists. (3) Updates the audit event builder so request_id and trace_id are set from context (best-effort) across all producers using the shared library.

Key behaviors / rules: - request_id: treated as a correlation token (not an auth token). We accept an inbound x-request-id only if it matches a conservative allowlist (length + charset). Otherwise we generate a new id and record a debug log. We always forward exactly one x-request-id downstream. - trace_id: derived from the active OTel span when present; otherwise left unset (schema allows null/omitted) to avoid creating fake trace IDs. - async/background jobs: when a job is enqueued from an HTTP request, we attach request_id and traceparent to the job payload headers so workers can restore correlation.

Scope: This PR touches the API gateway middleware, the control plane HTTP middleware used by tenant/config/policy/RBAC services, and the shared audit emitter library. Console UI / admin_action_id work is intentionally not included here (tracked separately), but this unblocks most of the cross-service correlation for sensitive actions.

Testing: Added unit tests for header parsing / sanitization, and integration tests that assert emitted audit events include request_id and trace_id when requests have trace context. Also validated locally against the audit exporter dev sink (events show consistent request_id across gateway -> control-plane).

Rollout/compat: No schema changes. Existing producers that don’t use the shared builder are unchanged (still tracked as gaps in ENG-4833). Exporter will see new fields populated more frequently; customers can safely ignore if not needed.

Follow-ups: - Apply the same middleware to remaining services that bypass the shared HTTP stack (runtime admin plane, some legacy internal tools). - Add enforcement (CI lint) to fail builds when sensitive-action code paths emit audit events without request_id (ENG-4831/PR-22071). - Add admin_action_id propagation for Console-triggered workflows (ENG-4830 follow-up + Console workstream).
commits: audit(correlation): add correlation context helpers (request_id, trace_id) and builders
gateway: generate/sanitize x-request-id and propagate downstream + response headers
control-plane: HTTP middleware to extract x-request-id + traceparent into request context
audit: populate request_id/trace_id in v1 event builder from context
jobs: attach correlation headers on enqueue and restore on worker execution
tests: add middleware parsing tests + integration coverage for correlation fields
ci_checks: integration tests (private fixtures): skipped (not required for this PR)
review_conversation: Allison Grant (review): Can we be explicit about which inbound headers we trust? Specifically, do we accept any x-request-id from customers, and could it blow up cardinality if someone sends a huge random string?

Caleb Johnson (author): Good call. Added sanitization: max length 64, [A-Za-z0-9-_], otherwise we generate a new one. Also added a metric counter audit_correlation.request_id_sanitized_total to track occurrences.
Sean Gallagher (review): For incident response, echoing x-request-id back to clients is helpful. Confirming we do it at the edge only and don’t accidentally override internal ids?

Caleb Johnson (author): Yes. Gateway is the canonical generator/normalizer. Downstream services only read from incoming context; they don’t regenerate unless the header is missing entirely (internal calls). Gateway always includes the header in response.
Hanae Suzuki (review): Any chance trace_id could contain sensitive data or become a stable identifier across tenants?

Caleb Johnson (author): trace_id is produced by OTel (random 16-byte) and not derived from tenant/user data. We’re not logging user identifiers into it. Also kept it best-effort (unset if no active span) to avoid inventing IDs.
Nadia Rahman (review): For async jobs, are we copying traceparent verbatim? Some producers might not have trace context (e.g., cron).

Caleb Johnson (author): We only attach traceparent if present; workers restore span context when available. For cron/background-only, request_id is generated per job run; trace_id remains unset unless the worker creates a span.
Ethan Park (review): Small nit: The control-plane middleware currently prefers x-request-id over a legacy header requestId. Should we keep legacy for a bit?

Caleb Johnson (author): Agreed. Added temporary fallback: requestId -> x-request-id with a deprecation log (once per process) so we can find remaining callers. Will remove after we update the last internal clients.
Logan Wright (review): Please add one integration assertion that the same request_id shows up across gateway event + downstream RBAC event in the same flow (helps coverage dashboard join logic).
Caleb Johnson (author): Added integration test: create API key via gateway -> control-plane; asserts both events share request_id, and trace_id is non-empty when traceparent is provided.
Marcus Lin (comment): Not a blocker, but what’s our stance on UUID vs ULID for request_id for sorting in SIEMs?

Caleb Johnson (author): Left as UUIDv4 for now to avoid changing existing assumptions; we can switch to ULID/UUIDv7 later as a separate change once exporter + docs are updated. This PR focuses on propagation and consistency.
